details: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained the federal funds rate target range at 3.75%-4.00% on October 28, 2026, following a 10-2 vote. The committee's statement acknowledged elevated uncertainty stemming from geopolitical developments, alongside robust economic activity and persistent inflation. While rates remained unchanged, the mention of geopolitical factors and the presence of dissenting votes favoring a hike suggest a cautious outlook and potential for future monetary tightening.
title: Fed Holds Rates Amid Geopolitical Uncertainty

details: The cryptocurrency industry has allocated approximately $176 million across more than 100 U.S. midterm election races in the current cycle. This significant financial outlay is part of a long-term strategy to cultivate a bipartisan network of allies in Congress. The goal is to shape future crypto regulation, aiming for a clear legislative framework for digital assets, especially in anticipation of a post-Trump era, following a "war on crypto" declaration by former President Trump in 2025.
title: Crypto Industry Spends $176M in US Midterms for Influence

details: Bitcoin experienced a reversal of gains, falling below the $80,000 threshold, as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East reportedly continued to restrain risk appetite. Reports indicated that the U.S. had advised several Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense military campaign after the midterm elections, contributing to investor caution. Concurrently, elevated Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data further complicated the prospect of immediate interest rate cuts, exerting additional downward pressure on cryptocurrencies and technology stocks.
title: Middle East Tensions and Inflation Dampen Bitcoin

details: The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, increased to 3.6% year-over-year in September 2026, up from 3.4% in August. The core PCE inflation rate, excluding volatile food and energy prices, also rose to 3.1% annually. Despite these inflationary pressures, the U.S. economy's real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew by a robust 3.37% in Q3 2026, an acceleration from the previous quarter. The combination of rising inflation and strong economic growth creates a complex picture for monetary policy, with inflation potentially pushing for tighter conditions, while growth indicates economic resilience.
title: US PCE Inflation Rises, Q3 GDP Strong
